^A.summary: Picks the font, rotation and size for the next text field. Place it right before ^FD so the text prints in that font instead of the default.

params.name: o
params.default: Last accepted ^FW value, or the ^FW default

^A@.summary: Selects a font by its file name in printer memory rather than by a one-letter name. Use it for downloaded or custom fonts.

^B0.summary: Aztec 2D bar code. Identical to ^BO and takes the same parameters.

params.name: b
params.default: 1 at 150 dpi, 2 at 200 dpi, 3 at 300 dpi, 6 at 600 dpi

params.name: f
params.description: Number of symbols for structured append

params.name: g
params.description: Optional ID field for structured append

^B1.summary: Code 11, a numeric symbology that also encodes the dash. Used mainly to label telecom equipment.

params.name: e
params.values: Y for one digit, N for two

^B2.summary: Interleaved 2 of 5, a compact numeric bar code that needs an even number of digits. Common on cartons and shipping cases.

params.name: e
params.description: Calculate and print a Mod 10 check digit

^B3.summary: Code 39 encodes uppercase letters, digits and a few symbols. It is widely used in industry and government labeling.

^B4.summary: Code 49, a stacked multi-row symbology that fits a lot of data in a small space.

params.name: h
params.description: Row height multiplier (this number times the module width gives each row height in dots)

params.name: f
params.values: N none, A above, B below

^B5.summary: USPS Planet Code, printed on mail pieces to track them through the postal system.

^B7.summary: PDF417, a stacked 2D symbology that holds large amounts of text or binary data. Common on ID cards and shipping labels.

params.name: h
params.description: Height of each row, in dots

^B8.summary: EAN-8, the short retail product code for small packages. Send 7 digits and the printer adds the check digit.

^B9.summary: UPC-E, a zero-suppressed form of UPC-A for small retail packages.

^BA.summary: Code 93, a denser alternative to Code 39 that can encode the full ASCII set.

^BB.summary: CODABLOCK, a stacked symbology built from rows of Code 39 or Code 128.

params.name: h
params.description: Height of each row, in dots

^BC.summary: Code 128, a dense symbology that encodes all ASCII characters. It is one of the most common bar codes on shipping and logistics labels.

params.name: m
params.values: N none, U UCC case, A automatic, D UCC/EAN

^BD.summary: UPS MaxiCode, a fixed-size 2D symbol with a bullseye center, used for package sorting.

^BE.summary: EAN-13, the standard retail product code outside North America. Send 12 digits and the printer adds the check digit.

^BF.summary: MicroPDF417, a smaller variant of PDF417 for moderate amounts of data.

params.name: h
params.default: Value set by ^BY, or 10 if there is none

^BI.summary: Industrial 2 of 5, an older numeric symbology. It is not very dense, so it mostly appears where existing systems require it.

^BJ.summary: Standard 2 of 5, a simple numeric symbology.

^BK.summary: ANSI Codabar, a numeric code framed by letter start and stop characters. Libraries, blood banks and parcel services use it.

^BL.summary: LOGMARS, the Code 39 variant used by the U.S. Department of Defense.

^BM.summary: MSI, a numeric symbology used mainly for shelf labels and inventory.

params.name: e
params.values: A none, B one Mod 10, C two Mod 10, D Mod 11 and Mod 10

params.name: e2
params.description: Show the check digit in the interpretation line

^BO.summary: Aztec, a square 2D symbol with a bullseye center. It needs no quiet zone and is common on transport tickets.

params.name: b
params.default: 1 at 150 dpi, 2 at 200 dpi, 3 at 300 dpi, 6 at 600 dpi

params.name: f
params.description: Number of symbols for structured append

params.name: g
params.description: Optional ID field for structured append

^BP.summary: Plessey, an older numeric symbology found on shelf and inventory labels.

^BQ.summary: QR Code. The field data starts with the error correction level and input mode, e.g. QA for level Q with automatic input.

params.name: c
params.default: 1 at 150 dpi, 2 at 200 dpi, 3 at 300 dpi, 6 at 600 dpi

^BR.summary: GS1 DataBar (formerly RSS). These compact symbols carry GTINs and extra data on small retail items such as produce.

params.name: e
params.description: Bar code height, in dots (some types only)

^BS.summary: UPC/EAN 2-digit or 5-digit add-on. Place it next to a UPC or EAN bar code for data such as magazine issue numbers.

^BT.summary: TLC39, a Code 39 symbol combined with a MicroPDF417 symbol, used in the telecommunications industry.

params.name: r1
params.description: Code 39 wide to narrow bar ratio

params.name: h1
params.default: 120 at 600 dpi, 60 at 300 dpi, 40 at 200 dpi

^BU.summary: UPC-A, the standard 12-digit retail product code in North America. Send 11 digits and the printer adds the check digit.

^BX.summary: Data Matrix, a square or rectangular 2D symbol that stores a lot of data in a small area. Common for marking parts and healthcare items.

params.name: h
params.description: Height of each module, in dots

params.name: g
params.default: _ on firmware V60.13.0.12 and later, ~ on older firmware

^BY.summary: Sets the default module width, wide to narrow ratio and height for the bar codes that follow. Put it before a bar code command to control its size.

^BZ.summary: USPS postal bar code: POSTNET by default, or PLANET or Intelligent Mail through the t parameter. It encodes ZIP Code and tracking data on mail.

^CC.summary: Changes the format command prefix from the caret (^) to another character. Use it when field data needs to contain carets.

~CC.summary: Same as ^CC, sent as a control command. Replaces the caret (^) format command prefix with another character.

^CD.summary: Changes the delimiter between command parameters from the comma to another character.

~CD.summary: Control command form of ^CD. Swaps the comma that separates command parameters for another character.

^CF.summary: Sets the default font and size for text fields that have no ^A command. Put it at the top of a label to avoid repeating ^A on every field.

params.name: w
params.default: 5, or the last permanently saved value

^CI.summary: Selects the character encoding used to read field data. Use ^CI28 to send UTF-8 text with accented or non-Latin characters.

params.name: s1,d1
params.description: Optional pairs that remap a source character to a destination

^CM.summary: Reassigns the letters that refer to the printer's memory devices (B:, E:, R: and A:).

params.name: a
params.description: Letter to use for B: memory
params.values: B, E, R, A or NONE

params.name: b
params.description: Letter to use for E: memory
params.values: B, E, R, A or NONE

params.name: c
params.description: Letter to use for R: memory
params.values: B, E, R, A or NONE

params.name: d
params.description: Letter to use for A: memory
params.values: B, E, R, A or NONE

params.name: e
params.values: M lets two letters point to the same device

^CO.summary: Turns the font cache on or off and sets how much extra memory it gets. Keeping scaled characters in the cache speeds up printing with scalable fonts.

params.name: b
params.description: Additional memory for the cache, in KB

^CT.summary: Changes the control command prefix from the tilde (~) to another character.

~CT.summary: Same as ^CT but sent as a control command. Replaces the tilde (~) control prefix with another character.

^CV.summary: Turns bar code data validation on or off. With validation on, the printer checks each bar code's data against its symbology and prints an error message in place of a bad code.

^CW.summary: Gives a font in printer memory a one-letter name that ^A can refer to. It can also replace one of the built-in font letters.

params.name: d:o.x
params.description: Drive, name and extension of the font

~DB.summary: Downloads a bitmap font to printer memory for use on labels.

params.name: d:o.x
params.description: Drive, name and extension of the font

params.name: base
params.description: Dots from the top of the cell to the baseline

params.name: space
params.description: Width of the space character, in dots

params.name: #char
params.description: Number of characters in the font

~DE.summary: Downloads a character encoding table (.DAT) to printer memory. Pair it with ^SE to map characters for TrueType fonts.

params.name: d:o.x
params.description: Drive, name and extension of the table

^DF.summary: Stores the rest of the format in printer memory as a reusable template instead of printing it. Mark the variable parts with ^FN, then print with ^XF.

params.name: d:o.x
params.description: Drive, name and extension of the stored format

~DG.summary: Downloads a graphic image to printer memory as hex data. Print it later with ^XG or ^IM.

params.name: d:o.x
params.description: Drive, name and extension of the graphic

params.name: t
params.description: Total number of bytes in the graphic

params.name: data
params.description: Image data, as ASCII hex (1 bits print black)

~DN.summary: Aborts a graphic download in progress, for example after the host sent the wrong amount of data.

~DS.summary: Downloads an Intellifont scalable font to printer memory.

params.name: d:o.x
params.description: Drive, name and extension of the font

params.name: s
params.description: Size of the font data, in bytes

~DT.summary: Downloads a bounded TrueType font (256 characters or fewer) to printer memory.

params.name: d:o.x
params.description: Drive, name and extension of the font

params.name: s
params.description: Size of the font data, in bytes

~DU.summary: Downloads an unbounded TrueType font to printer memory. Unbounded fonts have more than 256 characters, as Asian fonts do.

params.name: d:o.x
params.description: Drive, name and extension of the font

params.name: s
params.description: Size of the font data, in bytes

~DY.summary: General purpose download command on newer printers. It stores a file such as a graphic, PNG image, or TrueType or OpenType font in printer memory.

params.name: b
params.values: A ASCII hex or ZB64, B binary, C AR-compressed, P PNG (ZB64 encoded)

params.name: x
params.values: e.g. G graphic, P PNG, T TrueType

params.name: t
params.description: Total number of bytes in the file

params.name: w
params.description: Bytes per row for .GRF images (ignored for PNG and fonts)

~EG.summary: Erases all downloaded graphics from printer memory.

^FB.summary: Wraps a text field into a fixed-width block of several lines, for addresses and descriptions. A \& in the data forces a line break.

params.name: c
params.description: Extra space between lines, in dots

params.name: d
params.values: L left, C center, R right, J justified

params.name: e
params.description: Hanging indent of lines after the first, in dots

^FB.example:
^XA
^FO50,50^A0N,30,30^FB400,3,0,C,0^FDThis longer text wraps onto several centered lines^FS
^XZ

^FC.summary: Defines the characters that mark date and time placeholders in field data, such as %m or %H. The printer's real time clock fills them in at print time.

^FD.summary: Field data: the text to print or the value to encode in a bar code. It runs until the next ^FS.

^FH.summary: Enables hex codes in field data, written after an indicator character, e.g. _5E for a caret. Use it for ^, ~ or bytes that are hard to type.

^FM.summary: Positions each symbol when a PDF417 or MicroPDF417 bar code is split into several symbols (structured append).

params.name: x1,y1
params.description: Position of the first symbol, in dots

params.name: x2,y2
params.description: Position of the second symbol, and so on

^FN.summary: Numbers a field so it can be filled in later. Put it in a template saved with ^DF, then recall the template with ^XF and supply the data with ^FN and ^FD.

^FO.summary: Field origin: where the next field starts, measured from the label home (^LH). The position is the field's top left corner.

params.name: x
params.description: Distance from the left edge, in dots

params.name: y
params.description: Distance from the top, in dots

params.name: z
params.default: Last accepted ^FW value, or the ^FW default

^FP.summary: Prints a field's text vertically or in reverse order, and can add extra space between characters.

params.name: d
params.values: H horizontal, V vertical, R reverse

params.name: g
params.description: Extra gap between characters, in dots

^FR.summary: Reverses the field: wherever it overlaps something already drawn, dots flip between black and white. Use it for white text on a black box.

^FS.summary: Field separator. Every field definition, from ^FO through its data, ends with ^FS.

^FT.summary: Positions the next field like ^FO, but from the text baseline (bottom left) rather than the top left corner. Fields without a position continue after the previous one.

params.name: x
params.description: Distance from the left edge, in dots
params.default: Position after the last formatted text field

params.name: y
params.description: Distance from the top to the baseline, in dots
params.default: Position after the last formatted text field

params.name: z
params.default: Last accepted ^FW value, or the ^FW default

^FV.summary: Variable field data. It works like ^FD, but with ^MCN only ^FV fields are cleared between labels, so the rest of the image is reused.

^FW.summary: Sets the default rotation, and justification, for fields that don't specify their own. Handy for rotating all the text on a label at once.

params.name: z
params.default: Auto for ^TB, left for all other commands

^FX.summary: Comment. The printer ignores the text that follows, up to the next command.

^GB.summary: Draws a box or a line. Set the thickness equal to the height for a filled bar, or use a small height for a horizontal line.

^GC.summary: Draws a circle at the field origin.

^GD.summary: Draws a diagonal line across a box of the given width and height.

params.name: o
params.values: R or / right-leaning, L or \ left-leaning

^GE.summary: Draws an ellipse inside a box of the given width and height.

^GF.summary: Prints a bitmap image straight from data in the format, without storing it first. It is the usual way to put a logo or image on a label.

params.name: a
params.values: A ASCII hex, B binary, C compressed binary

params.name: b
params.description: Number of data bytes sent (equals c for ASCII hex)

^GS.summary: Prints a special symbol chosen by the field data letter: A registered, B copyright, C trademark, D UL, E CSA.

~HB.summary: Requests the battery status of a battery-powered printer.

~HD.summary: Requests printhead diagnostic information from the printer.

^HF.summary: Returns a stored format to the host as ZPL text, which shows what a ^DF template contains.

params.name: d:o.x
params.description: Drive, name and extension of the stored format

^HG.summary: Uploads a stored graphic to the host as hex data.

params.name: d:o.x
params.description: Drive, name and extension of the graphic
params.default: Drive by search priority, name UNKNOWN

^HH.summary: Returns the printer's configuration to the host as text, with the same information as the configuration label.

~HI.summary: Printer identification. The reply gives the model, firmware version, resolution, memory size and installed options.

~HM.summary: Reports RAM status: total, maximum available and currently available memory.

~HS.summary: Host status request. The printer answers with three strings that report conditions such as paper out, pause, head open, ribbon out and labels remaining in the batch.

~HU.summary: Returns the printer's ZebraNet Alert settings to the host.

^HV.summary: Returns the data of a numbered field (set with ^FN or ^RF) to the host, with an optional header. Often used with RFID to check what was read or written.

params.name: h
params.description: Header text to send before the data

params.name: t
params.description: Termination text to send after the data

params.name: a
params.values: F once per format, L once per label printed

^HW.summary: Lists the objects stored in printer memory and sends the list to the host.

params.name: d:o.x
params.description: Drive and name pattern to list

^HY.summary: Uploads a graphic from printer memory to the host.

params.name: d:o.x
params.description: Drive, name and extension of the graphic

^HZ.summary: Returns description information as XML: format settings, the object directory, object data or printer status.

params.name: b
params.values: a all, f format settings, l object directory, o object data, r printer status

^ID.summary: Deletes stored objects such as graphics, fonts or formats from printer memory. Wildcards (*) are allowed.

params.name: d:o.x
params.description: Drive, name and extension of the object to delete

^IL.summary: Loads a stored image as the label background, starting at the top left corner, and prints later fields on top. Use it with ^IS to build a reusable form.

params.name: d:o.x
params.description: Drive, name and extension of the stored image

^IM.summary: Places a stored graphic at the field origin, like ^XG but without magnification. Skipping the scaling can take less formatting time than ^XG.

params.name: d:o.x
params.description: Drive, name and extension of the stored graphic
params.default: Drive by search priority, name UNKNOWN

^IS.summary: Saves the label built so far as an image in printer memory. Store a form once, then load it with ^IL on later labels.

params.name: d:o.x
params.description: Drive, name and extension of the image to save

~JA.summary: Cancels every format waiting in the printer's buffer, along with any batch that is printing. The printer stops once the current label finishes.

^JB.summary: Initializes (erases and formats) a flash memory device.

params.name: a
params.values: A option flash, B flash card, E internal flash

~JB.summary: Resets (erases) optional memory, on printers that have it.

~JC.summary: Media sensor calibration. The printer feeds labels to learn the label length and set its sensors.

~JD.summary: Starts communications diagnostics mode, in which the printer prints every character it receives along with its hex value and any communication errors. Useful for debugging what the host is sending.

~JE.summary: Ends the communications diagnostics mode started by ~JD and returns the printer to normal operation.

~JF.summary: Sets whether a battery-powered printer pauses when the battery voltage is low.

params.name: p
params.values: Y or N (N is suggested when running from a car battery adapter)

~JG.summary: Prints a graph of the media sensor readings, which helps show why the printer misdetects labels or gaps.

^JJ.summary: Configures the auxiliary port that connects an applicator or other external device.

~JL.summary: Sets the label length by feeding labels until the printer finds it. Run it after changing media.

^JM.summary: Sets print density: ^JMA is full density, and ^JMB halves it (8 dots/mm becomes 4, for example), doubling the size of everything on the label, ^FO positions included. Place it before the first ^FS in the format, and the setting stays in effect.

params.name: n
params.values: A full resolution, B half resolution

~JN.summary: Makes the printhead test fatal. If the test finds a bad element, the printer stops and reports an error.

~JO.summary: Makes the printhead test non-fatal, which is the default. A failed test shows an error and stops printing, but PAUSE continues without a power cycle, unlike with ~JN.

~JP.summary: Cancels the format being processed and puts the printer in Pause Mode, like pressing CANCEL on the printer. Each further ~JP clears the next format in the buffer.

~JR.summary: Resets the printer as if it had been power cycled. Unsaved settings are lost.

^JS.summary: Selects which media sensor the printer uses to detect labels.

params.name: a
params.values: A auto, R reflective, T transmissive
params.default: A on Z series, R on S4M

~JS.summary: Controls when the printer backfeeds labels after tear-off or peel-off, as a percentage before and after printing.

params.name: b
params.values: A 100% after printing, B 100% before the next label, N normal (90% after), O off, or 10 to 90 in steps of 10 (percent done after printing)

^JT.summary: Sets how often the printer runs its automatic printhead test, counted in labels.

params.description: Number of labels between head tests

params.name: a
params.description: Choose the range of elements to test yourself

params.name: b
params.description: First element to test when a is Y

params.name: c
params.description: Last element to test when a is Y

^JU.summary: Saves the current settings to permanent memory, or reloads saved or factory settings.

params.name: a
params.description: Configuration action (reloaded defaults are lost at power off unless saved with ^JUS)
params.values: A factory and factory network defaults, F factory defaults, N factory network defaults, R recall last saved, S save current

^JW.summary: Ribbon tension, on printers where it is adjustable.

params.name: t
params.values: L low, M medium, H high

~JX.summary: Cancels a format that was only partly received, for example after the host connection dropped mid-format.

^JZ.summary: Sets whether the printer reprints a label that failed because of an error such as paper out or ribbon out.

~KB.summary: Puts a battery-powered printer into battery discharge mode to condition the battery.

^KD.summary: Selects the date and time format shown on the configuration label and display, on printers with a real time clock.

params.name: a
params.values: 0 version number, 1 to 4 MM/DD/YY or DD/MM/YY in 12 or 24 hour time

^KL.summary: Language shown on the printer's control panel.

^KN.summary: Sets the printer's network name and description, which appear on its configuration label and web page. Send ^JUS to save them.

params.name: a
params.default: ZBRxxx, where xxx comes from the MAC address

^KP.summary: Password that protects the printer's front panel settings.

params.name: a
params.default: 1234 (empty on printers bought in EMEA after August 1, 2025)

^LH.summary: Moves the label home, the 0,0 point that all field positions are measured from. Shift a whole design this way without editing every ^FO.

^LL.summary: Sets the label length (height), which continuous media requires. Put it before the first ^FS so it affects the current label.

params.name: y
params.default: Set on the LCD, or the printer's maximum label length

params.name: x
params.values: Y all media, N continuous media only

^LR.summary: Reverses every field that follows, as if each had ^FR, so black and white flip where fields overlap.

^LS.summary: Shifts all fields to the left by a number of dots. Used mainly for compatibility with older printers.

^LT.summary: Moves the whole label image up or down relative to the label's top edge. Corrects vertical alignment without changing field positions.

params.name: x
params.values: -120 to 120 on most printers (negative moves the format toward the top)

^MC.summary: Controls whether the label image is cleared after printing. With ^MCN the image is kept, so the next label only redraws its ^FV fields.

^MD.summary: Adjusts print darkness for the labels that follow, relative to the current darkness setting.

^MF.summary: Sets what the printer does with the media at power up and when the printhead is closed, such as feeding a label or calibrating.

params.name: p
params.values: F feed, C calibrate, L length, N none, S short calibration

^ML.summary: Maximum label length the printer searches through when it calibrates and looks for a gap or mark.

params.name: a
params.description: Maximum label length, in dot rows

^MM.summary: Print mode: what the printer does with a label after printing it, such as tear-off, peel-off, rewind or cut.

params.name: a
params.values: e.g. T tear-off, P peel-off, R rewind, A applicator, C cutter

^MN.summary: Tells the printer which kind of media it has, continuous, gap (web) or black mark, so it can find the start of each label.

params.name: a
params.values: N continuous, Y or W gap/notch (web sensing), M black mark, A auto-detect (G-series only), V continuous with variable length (KR403 only)

params.name: b
params.description: Black mark offset, in dots (used only when a is M)

^MP.summary: Disables front panel functions, such as darkness or position adjustment, so operators can't change them.

params.name: a
params.values: e.g. D darkness, P position, C calibration, E enable all

^MT.summary: Chooses the printing method: thermal transfer, with a ribbon, or direct thermal, on heat-sensitive media without one.

params.name: a
params.values: T thermal transfer, D direct thermal

^MU.summary: Sets the units for positions and sizes: dots, inches or millimeters. It can also convert a format designed for one resolution to another.

params.name: a
params.values: D dots, I inches, M millimeters

^MW.summary: Turns the printhead cold warning on or off.

~NC.summary: Connects to one printer on a shared serial (RS-485) network, selected by its network ID.

^NI.summary: Gives the printer a network ID number for use on a shared serial (RS-485) network.

~NR.summary: Makes every printer on a shared serial network transparent, so all of them receive the data that follows.

^NS.summary: Changes the printer's wired network settings, such as how it gets an IP address, the IP address, subnet mask and gateway.

params.name: a
params.values: A all, B BOOTP, C DHCP and BOOTP, D DHCP, G gleaning only, R RARP, P permanent

~NT.summary: Makes the currently connected printer on a shared serial network transparent.

^PF.summary: Slews the media: feeds it forward by a number of dot rows without printing, measured from the bottom of the label.

params.description: Number of dot rows to slew

^PH.summary: Feeds a blank label to the start of the next label (the home position) as part of a format.

~PH.summary: Control command version of ^PH. Feeds a blank label to the start of the next label, the home position.

^PM.summary: Prints the whole label as a mirror image, flipped left to right.

^PO.summary: Rotates the whole label 180 degrees, for when labels come out of the printer upside down relative to how you want them.

^PP.summary: Pauses the printer after the current format prints. The pause is not immediate, so several labels may print first, and the printer resumes when PAUSE is pressed or ~PS is sent.

~PP.summary: Pauses the printer once the current label finishes printing. Pressing PAUSE or sending ~PS resumes it.

^PQ.summary: Print quantity: how many copies of the label to print, and optionally when to pause and how many times to repeat each serial number.

^PR.summary: Sets the print, slew and backfeed speeds. Slower speeds usually give better print quality.

params.name: p
params.values: e.g. 2 to 14 (inches per second) or A to E

~PR.summary: Reprints the last label, like an applicator's reprint signal. Works only when reprint is enabled.

~PS.summary: Resumes printing on a paused printer, for example after ^PP or ~PP, with the same effect as pressing the PAUSE button.

^PW.summary: Print width of the label. Set it so content isn't cut off or placed off the label when the media is narrower than the printhead.

~RO.summary: Resets one of the printer's advanced counters, such as a user label counter or an RFID label counter.

params.name: c
params.values: 1 or 2 user counters, 3 valid RFID, 4 voided RFID, C head cleaned, R head replaced and head cleaned (C and R on some models only)

^SC.summary: Configures the serial port: baud rate, data bits, parity, stop bits and handshake.

params.name: c
params.values: N none, E even, O odd

params.name: e
params.values: X XON/XOFF, D DTR/DSR, R RTS, M DTR/DSR XON/XOFF (G-Series only)

params.name: f
params.values: A ACK/NAK, N none, Z Zebra

~SD.summary: Sets print darkness, the same setting as darkness on the front panel.

^SE.summary: Selects the stored encoding table (a .DAT file) the printer uses to map characters.

^SF.summary: Makes part of a field's data count up or down on each label printed. A mask sets which characters change and how, e.g. D for decimal digits and % to skip a character.

params.name: a
params.values: D decimal, H hex, O octal, A alpha, N alphanumeric, % skip

^SL.summary: Sets the real time clock mode, which prints either the time the format was received or the time each label prints, and the language for printed date and time text.

params.name: a
params.values: S start time, T time now, or 1 to 999 seconds of tolerance

params.name: b
params.values: 1 English, 2 Spanish, 3 French, 4 German, 5 Italian, up to 18 Polish
params.default: Language set with ^KL or on the control panel

^SN.summary: Serial number that counts up or down on each label. It takes the place of ^FD and works with ^PQ to print a run of labels.

^SO.summary: Offsets the secondary or third clock from the real time clock, e.g. to print a best-before date 30 days ahead.

^SP.summary: Starts printing the part of the label formatted so far while the printer keeps receiving the rest. Speeds up long labels.

params.name: a
params.description: Dot row at which to start printing

^SQ.summary: Stops a ZebraNet alert from being sent.

^SR.summary: Printhead resistance value. Newer printer models set it automatically.

params.description: Resistance, four digits (use a value no higher than the one shown on the printhead, or you may damage it)

^SS.summary: Media, web and ribbon sensor values, set directly. The printer normally sets these itself during calibration.

^ST.summary: Date and time for the printer's real time clock.

^SX.summary: Sets up a ZebraNet alert, so the printer notifies a destination such as an email address when a condition like paper out occurs.

params.name: a
params.values: e.g. paper out or ribbon out

params.name: c
params.description: Alert when the condition is set

^SZ.summary: Selects the ZPL version the printer interprets: ZPL or ZPL II.

~TA.summary: Adjusts where the media stops for tear-off or peel-off, relative to the default position.

params.values: -120 to 120, always as three digits (e.g. 020) or the command is ignored

^TO.summary: Copies an object, such as a graphic or format, from one memory device to another. Wildcards (*) are allowed.

params.name: d:o.x
params.default: Name and extension of the source object

~WC.summary: Prints a configuration label listing the printer's current settings.

^WD.summary: Prints a label listing the objects stored in printer memory, such as fonts, graphics and formats.

params.name: d:o.x
params.description: Drive and name pattern to list

^XA.summary: Opens a label format. Every label begins with ^XA and ends with ^XZ.

^XB.summary: Suppresses the feed to the tear-off or peel-off position after the label, so no backfeed is needed before the next one. For printing labels back to back.

^XF.summary: Recalls a format stored with ^DF. Follow it with ^FN and ^FD pairs to fill in the template's numbered fields.

params.name: d:o.x
params.description: Drive, name and extension of the stored format
params.default: Drive by search priority, name UNKNOWN

^XG.summary: Prints a stored graphic at the field origin, with optional magnification.

params.name: d:o.x
params.description: Drive, name and extension of the stored graphic
params.default: Drive by search priority, name UNKNOWN

^XZ.summary: Closes a label format. The printer prints the label when it reaches ^XZ.

^ZZ.summary: Puts a battery-powered printer (PA400 or PT400) to sleep after it has been idle for a set time.

params.name: b
params.values: Y shuts down even if labels are still queued, N waits until all labels are printed
